nodes.description: With the brake partly released, sarcoplasmic reticulum calcium reuptake is faster and basal contractility rises, as in a heart under continuous beta-adrenergic stimulation. Calcium transients in human heterozygous myocardium have not been measured.

nodes.description: Dephosphorylated phospholamban lowers the calcium affinity of SERCA2a, and its phosphorylation by protein kinase A or CaMKII during beta-adrenergic stimulation lifts that brake. ClinGen frames the shared mechanism of all PLN-related cardiomyopathy as dysregulated SERCA2 function and calcium handling.

nodes.description: The best-characterised CMH18 lesion is the heterozygous nonsense allele c.116T>G, p.Leu39Ter (L39X, L39stop), which truncates phospholamban within its second transmembrane segment. Expressed in cells, the truncated protein is barely detectable, does not inhibit SERCA2a, and is misrouted away from the sarcoplasmic reticulum when it is made; co-expression with wild-type phospholamban shows no dominant-negative effect. A heterozygote therefore carries roughly half the normal amount of functional phospholamban.

nodes.description: Seven HCM probands in three cohorts carried rare single-nucleotide variants in the PLN promoter that were absent from controls. In reporter assays -77A>G raised promoter activity in neonatal rat cardiomyocytes, whereas -42C>G lowered it by 43-47% in C6 and C2C12 cells; five further promoter variants found in the Mayo cohort have no functional data. If the reporter results hold in the heart, these alleles would move phospholamban expression, and with it SERCA2a inhibition, in opposite directions. The node is HYPOTHETICAL: each variant rests on a single family or proband, none has been shown to alter phospholamban protein in human myocardium, and their causal role in HCM is not established.
